ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, the curve is the position-time (y-t) graph of a particle moving along the y axis. Let vertically upward be the positive direction of the y axis. It is known that the graph is a parabola, so from the graph it can be known that
A. At time t＝0 the velocity of the particle is 0
B. During the time 0～$0{\sim}_{t_1}$ the particle moves in the negative direction of the y axis
C. During the time $0{\sim}t_2$ the velocity of the particle continuously decreases
D. During the time $t_1\sim_{t_3}$ the displacement of the particle relative to the coordinate origin O is first positive and then negative

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis is y, with the positive direction upward; the horizontal axis is t. The position-time graph is a downward-opening parabola, and the curve reaches the highest point Hm at t2, which is marked by a dashed line in the figure; from t1 to t2, the curve rises upward with time; from t2 to t3, the curve descends downward with time, and returns to the y=0 axis near t3. Reasoning: In a y-t graph, the ordinate y represents the position of the particle relative to the coordinate origin O. Looking at the graph by intervals, from t1 to t2, the y coordinate increases, indicating that the particle undergoes displacement in the positive y direction, and the displacement is positive; from t2 to t3, the y coordinate decreases, indicating that the particle undergoes displacement in the negative y direction, and the displacement is negative. Therefore, during the time from t1 to t3, the displacement of the particle relative to the coordinate origin O is first positive and then negative.
